HISTORICAL PRE-VERIFICATION SOURCE NOTE:
IMAGE 10 OF THE OWNER'S BRIEF OF 2026-08-18, identified. The brief describes it as "The Sauganash (Trowbridge drawing). Adds: louvred shutters on the sash, the tall board fence enclosing the rear yard, a saddled horse at the post (L1: reference only), the log wing's door direct to grade." The plate at this locator was retrieved and read on 2026-08-22 and carries all four: louvred shutters flanking every window of the clapboard block, a tall vertical-board fence running off to the right behind the building, a saddled horse standing at a post at the right-hand road edge, and the log wing's door opening straight onto the ground with no step or platform. It also carries the two posts at the road edge and the log wing under its own shingled roof that the brief's images 8 and 9 give.

UNDATED, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GUESSED. The signature carries what appears to be a two-digit year after the name, as the Green Tree drawing's does, and it is not legible at the resolution published here. The companion is signed 1902 and the two are plainly one campaign, but this record does not assert a date the plate does not give: `date` says undated, and any use that turns on the year must resolve it first.

IT IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT WITNESS OF THE 1831 BUILDING. docs/RESEARCH/sauganash_hotel.md § 4 already treats the Braunhold engraving in Andreas and the Kurz & Allison panel as one witness and a copy; this drawing is a third view in the same descent, and the caution there applies here in full. What it adds is DETAIL the other two do not draw — the shutters and the fence — at the cost of being the latest and least direct of them.

WHAT THE PROJECT ALREADY TOOK FROM IT, by path: the Sauganash's louvred shutters (docs/LIBERTIES.md, the weakest of the three plate readings by the record's own note), the board fence at the rear yard, and the hitching posts at the road edge in data/frontage/sauganash_frontage.json.
